notes.text:
This update for poppler, poppler-qt5 fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-93313: JBIG2 stream processing can cause integer overflows (bsc#1282532).
- CVE-2026-93314: TrueType font processing can cause integer overflows (bsc#1282531).
- CVE-2026-102620: Data corruption via integer overflow in FoFiTrueType:cvtSfnts (bsc#1283330).
- CVE-2026-102621: Denial of Service via integer overflow in SplashClip (bsc#1283331).
- CVE-2026-107705: Denial of Service via stack-based buffer overflow in PDF decryption (bsc#1284844).

Such manipulation leads to integer overflow. The attack can only be performed from a local environment. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 26.09.0 is able to address this issue. The name of the patch is 323c91036d99926a8b90dc14329f7b40aece22f8. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

notes.text: Poppler 0.42.0 through 26.10.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow in Decrypt::revision6Hash() that allows attackers controlling the password to overwrite stack memory when opening AESV3/R6 encrypted PDFs. Attackers can supply a password longer than 127 bytes through applications using the libpoppler, libpoppler-glib or C++ API to overflow the K1 and E buffers, crashing the process or corrupting memory.
